excerpt:
The world of work is changing faster than ever.

Technology is transforming how people learn, communicate, work, create businesses and access opportunities. For today's students, academic education remains essential, but it must increasingly be complemented by practical digital and employment skills.
title: Preparing Students and Teachers for a Digital Future: The Case for Digital Skills Clubs in Schools
body:
The question schools should therefore be asking is not only:

“Are our students prepared for their examinations?”

It is also:

“Are our students prepared for the world they will enter after school?”

This is where the SheIsConnected Digital Skills Club comes in.

Preparing Students Beyond the Classroom

Students need opportunities to understand how technology can be used beyond entertainment and social media.

Digital skills can help students become more confident learners, creators and future professionals.

Through practical training, students can learn how to:

Use digital productivity tools to support their studies.
Create professional documents and presentations.
Design digital content and communicate ideas visually.
Research information and assess whether online information is reliable.
Use email and other professional communication tools.
Work collaboratively on digital projects.
Understand the basics of coding and technology.
Explore artificial intelligence and emerging technologies responsibly.
Build digital portfolios that demonstrate what they can do.
Develop CVs and understand basic employment preparation.
Identify online learning and career opportunities.

The objective is not simply to teach students how to use computers.

The objective is to help students use technology to learn, create, solve problems and access opportunities.

From Digital Literacy to Employability

A student may leave school with good examination results but still struggle to navigate the digital requirements of further education or employment.

Digital employability skills can help bridge that gap.

Students can be introduced to practical areas such as:

Professional communication — writing emails, communicating appropriately online and presenting ideas.

Digital productivity — using documents, spreadsheets, presentations and collaborative platforms.

Personal branding — understanding how to present their skills and achievements professionally.

Career readiness — preparing CVs, portfolios and applications.

Problem-solving — using technology to research and develop solutions to real-world challenges.

Continuous learning — knowing how to find and use online resources to keep developing new skills.

These capabilities can remain valuable regardless of the career a student eventually chooses.

Teachers Must Keep Learning Too

There is another group that must be part of this conversation: teachers.

Teachers are our number-one supporters in preparing young people for the future.

A school cannot effectively prepare students for a changing digital world if teachers are not given opportunities to understand that world themselves.

This does not mean every teacher needs to become a technology specialist.

It means teachers should have opportunities to continuously update their knowledge and understand the technologies, skills and ways of working that are becoming relevant to their students.

Teachers can benefit from developing skills in:

Digital teaching and collaboration tools.
Artificial intelligence awareness.
Digital content creation.
Online research and information literacy.
Cybersecurity and responsible technology use.
Digital communication.
Data and productivity tools.
New approaches to student engagement.
Understanding emerging workplace skills.
Teachers as Role Models for Lifelong Learning

One of the most important lessons a teacher can give a student does not come from a textbook.

It comes from example.

When students see their teachers learning new technologies, experimenting with new approaches and updating their knowledge, they learn that education does not stop at graduation.

The message becomes:

“If the world changes, I can learn and adapt.”

This is one of the most important capabilities we can develop in young people.

Introducing the SheIsConnected Digital Skills Club

To support this vision, SheIsConnected proposes the establishment of Digital Skills Clubs in schools.

The clubs will provide a practical platform where students can participate in workshops focused on digital skills, employability and future opportunities.

Rather than relying only on traditional classroom teaching, the clubs can use practical, project-based learning.
